The '''Boys of Corus''' were a [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] band from the [[Corus system/Legends|Corus system]]. Among their membership was the [[Lepi/Legends|Lepi]] [[Jaxxon/Legends|Jaxxon]], who learned his marksmanship while doing jobs with the group. However, on a mission to the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]], they were double-crossed, and the band was scattered.<ref name="Gamer4" /> One of Jaxxon's rivals, a [[H'nemthe (species)/Legends|H'nemthe]] named [[Dafi (bounty hunter)|Dafi]], lost his [[Starship/Legends|starship]] and a [[Limb/Legends|finger]] on each hand in the botched Corporate Sector run, blaming Jaxxon for it and turning from rivalry to bitter enmity.<ref name="TNSM7">{{SW|url=news/the-not-so-magnificent-seven|text=The Not-So Magnificent Seven|int=The Not-So Magnificent Seven|nolive=1}}</ref> The disastrous mission put an end to the Boys of Corus, and they disbanded, going their separate ways. After leaving the group, Jaxxon returned to [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] and pursued a career as a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]], eventually buying the [[Rabbit's Foot/Legends|''Rabbit's Foot'']].<ref name="Gamer4" />

==Behind the scenes==
The "boys of Corus" is a reference by "[[The Starhoppers of Aduba-3]]" author [[Pablo Hidalgo]] to [[Wikipedia:Bugs Bunny|Bugs Bunny]], the cartoon character that Jaxxon was based upon. The name is an allusion to the "Boys of the Chorus," a memorable line which Bugs Bunny sings several times in the [[Wikipedia:Looney Tunes|Looney Tunes]] short, ''[[Wikipedia:What's Up, Doc? (1950 film)|What's Up, Doc?]]''.<ref name="Pablog 60">{{Blog|pablog|60|Tales of the Big Green Bunny: Behind the Scenes of Gamer #4 &mdash; The Coachella Valley, and the Giant Carrot Festival}}</ref>
